summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(a) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 for deciding the NAPAF and consequent adjudication of disputes under the PPA dated 7.5.2004 between Punjab State Power Corporation Limited and NHPC Limited in respect of Parbati Hydroelectric Project-III. Punjab State Power Corporation Limited The Mall, Patiala, Punjab - 147001 ** Petitioner** _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_1_** _of_ **_8_** _a) Direct NHPC to reimburse to the Petitioner the excess capacity charges billed to the Petitioner as per the details mentioned in Annexure G;_ _b) Direct NHPC to strictly adhere to the NAPAF decided by this Hon’ble Commission in its various Orders while billing the capacity charges to the Petitioner;_ _d) Award the costs of the present litigation in favour of the Petitioner and against NHPC;_ _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_2_** _of_ **_8_** 3. During the pendency of Petition No.96/GT/2020, PSPCL has filed the present Petition, seeking the relief(s) as in para 1 above, based on the following submissions: _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_3_** _of_ **_8_** (b) At the time of filing the present appeal, the truing up for Parbati-III HEP for the period 2014-19 and the tariff petition for the period 2019-24 (Petition No. 96/GT/2020) have been filed and are pending before this Commission. The Petitioner is also raising the issue of NAPAF as a response to the above petitions. However, the present petition is being filed due to the methodology adopted by NHPC for the computation of capacity charges in the provisional and supplementary (for AFC revisions) energy bills raised by it, as the methodology so adopted is in direct contravention of the orders of the Hon’ble Commission. _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_4_** _of_ **_8_** 5. The Petition was heard on ‘admission’ on 23.11.2021. On a specific observation by the Commission that the present petition may not be kept pending, considering the fact that the issues raised in the present petition, were raised by the Petitioner, PSPCL, in its reply to Petition No.96/GT/2020 (filed by Respondent NHPC), which was pending for consideration, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, PSCPL, requested that the present petition may be kept pending, till the final disposal of Petition No.96/GT/2020. Accordingly, based on the consent of the parties, the present petition was directed to be listed after the disposal of Petition No. 96/GT/2020. 6. Thereafter, the Commission, vide its order dated 31.3.2024 in Petition No.96/ GT/2020, revised the tariff of the generating station, after a truing-up exercise for the _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_5_** _of_ **_8_** period 2014-19, and also approved the tariff for the period 2019-24. In the said order, - 2024) seeking review of the aforesaid order dated 31.3.2024, on the following grounds: 8. Subsequently, the Commission, after hearing the parties, rejected the aforesaid _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_6_** _of_ **_8_** _With regard to the submissions of the Review Petitioner that the Respondent NHPC adopted an incorrect methodology for the computation of the capacity charges in the energy bills, we note that similar issues were raised by the Review Petitioner in the original petition and mentioned in para 77 of the impugned order and the same was considered and disposed of vide para 78 of the impugned order. The Review Petitioner, in our view, has sought to reargue the case on merits, which cannot be permitted in review. Accordingly, we find no error apparent on the face of the impugned order warranting review of the impugned order on this count. Therefore, the review on this count is rejected_ .” 10. As stated, the present Petition was kept pending till a final decision was taken in Petition No. 96/GT/2020, wherein the issue of NAPAF was raised by PSCPL, which was pending for consideration. Pursuant to the disposal of Petition No.96/GT/2020, wherein, the issue of NAPAF (raised by PSPCL) was also decided vide order dated 31.3.2024, PSPCL filed Review Petition (Petition No. 22/RP/2024) raising the issue of NAPAF, which was also decided and rejected by the Commission vide order dated 24.2.2025. Since the issue of NAPAF raised by the Petitioner PSPCL in the present Petition and the reliefs sought thereof, had already been examined and considered by the Commission in its orders dated 31.3.2024 and 24.2.2025, as stated above, nothing survives for the consideration of the Commission in the present petition. Accordingly, the present petition is disposed of as infructuous. _Order in Petition No. 153/MP/2021 Page_ **_7_** _of_ **_8_**
